- Hi @username_0 , the error `FATAL: resolved path /containers/sarek-latest.simg doesn't match with opened path /containers/sarek-latest.simg (deleted)` say the image (`/containers/sarek-latest.simg`) was deleted (`/containers/sarek-latest.simg (deleted)`) during singularity execution, which is really weird. Can you please paste a reproducer for this issue ?
- Closing, feel free to re-open if you still have this issue @username_0
- One of our users ran across this issue with a SLURM job array. I've been able to reproduce the error with singularity 3.5.2-1.1.osg34.el6 on EL6 (2.6.32-754.27.1.el6.x86_64) by starting several simultaneous singularity instances from the same image. ``` singularity pull docker://godlovedc/lolcow for i in `seq 1 10` ; do singularity run lolcow_latest.sif > /dev/null & done wait ``` I was not able to reproduce with singularity 3.5.2-1.1.osg34.el7 on EL7. I suspect making a copy of the sif before starting each job will avoid the problem on EL6.

- I recently discussed this in a slack as well. There (on a version reporting as 3.0.2-1.el7), they can consistently trigger it. I asked one of them observing it to run a reasonably tight (1 second sleeps) loop with `stat -c %i FILE` to get the inode as well as observe any issues in accessing the name. In that situation, the inode did not change (so it was the same file all along) and they saw no issues stating the name (so I believe it was there during the entire run). This is also with sarek (a nextflow pipeline). From what I understood from that discussion, it also seems to be related to the amount of singularity processes running simultaneously using that container file (unclear to me whatever that was locally only or in the complete cluster).

Title:
Singularity fails to mount cephfs with kernel driver. no parent mount point found

Description:
### Version of Singularity: What version of Singularity are you using? Run: ``` $ singularity version 3.5.2-1.1.el7 ``` <!-- please include command-line output in a code block --> ### Expected behavior What did you expect to see when you do...? Singularity fails to start with `no parent mount point found` if we use CEPH Kernel driver [1][2]. Once I have changed to use CEPH Fuse Client [3] or [4], it works. ``` bin/singularity --debug exec --home /wntmp/condor/execute/dir_37905/glide_0hLVwO/:/srv --bind /mnt/hadoop --bind /storage --bind /cvmfs --pwd /srv --contain --ipc --pid /cvmfs/singularity.opensciencegrid.org/cmssw/cms:rhel6 bash ``` ``` [1] $ df -h | grep storage 10.3.11.157:6789,10.3.16.147:6789,10.3.11.198:6789,10.3.10.12:6789,10.3.13.102:6789,10.3.16.148:6789:/ 114T 56T 58T 49% /storage [2] /etc/fstab # Failing one 10.3.11.157:6789,10.3.16.147:6789,10.3.11.198:6789,10.3.10.12:6789,10.3.13.102:6789,10.3.16.148:6789:/ /storage ceph name=admin,secretfile=/etc/ceph/client.key,_netdev 0 2 [3] /etc/fstab # Successful one none /storage fuse.ceph ceph.id=admin,ceph.conf=/etc/ceph/ceph.conf,_netdev 0 2 [4] /etc/fstab # Successful one 10.3.11.157:6789,10.3.16.147:6789,10.3.11.198:6789,10.3.10.12:6789,10.3.13.102:6789,10.3.16.148:6789:/ /storage fuse.ceph ceph.id=admin,ceph.conf=/etc/ceph/ceph.conf,_netdev 0 2 ``` ### Actual behavior What actually happend? Why was it incorrect? ``` $ cat sing_star_output | grep storage DEBUG [U=0,P=37021] prepareAutofs() Could not keep file descriptor for user bind path /storage: no mount point DEBUG [U=0,P=37010] addUserbindsMount() Adding /storage to mount list DEBUG [U=0,P=37010] mountGeneric() Mounting /var/singularity/mnt/session/rootfs/storage to /var/singularity/mnt/session/underlay/storage FATAL [U=0,P=37010] Master() container creation failed: mount /storage->/storage error: while mounting /storage: while getting mount flags for /storage: while searching parent mount point entry for /storage: no parent mount point found ``` <!-- if this is a feature request, you can ignore this next part --> ### Steps to reproduce this behavior How can others reproduce this issue/problem? Latest singularity and cephfs. ``` $ yum list installed | grep ceph ceph-common.x86_64 2:13.2.6-0.el7 @Ceph ceph-fuse.x86_64 2:13.2.6-0.el7 @Ceph libcephfs2.x86_64 2:13.2.6-0.el7 @Ceph python-cephfs.x86_64 2:13.2.6-0.el7 @Ceph ``` ### What OS/distro are you running ``` $ cat /etc/os-release NAME="CentOS Linux" VERSION="7 (Core)" ID="centos" ID_LIKE="rhel fedora" VERSION_ID="7" PRETTY_NAME="CentOS Linux 7 (Core)" ANSI_COLOR="0;31" CPE_NAME="cpe:/o:centos:centos:7" HOME_URL="https://www.centos.org/" BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugs.centos.org/" CENTOS_MANTISBT_PROJECT="CentOS-7" CENTOS_MANTISBT_PROJECT_VERSION="7" REDHAT_SUPPORT_PRODUCT="centos" REDHAT_SUPPORT_PRODUCT_VERSION="7" ``` ### How did you install Singularity Write here how you installed Singularity. Eg. RPM, source. `yum install singularity`

Comments:
- I think this is the difference between fuse, and the standard cephfs ... IIRC, cephfs does some, non-standard stuff to make it work they way they wanted distributed. @cclerget I think this would be similar to BTRFS where there was a virtual device on a subvolume. Ceph did some weird stuff when mounting a volume directly... It has been a few years since I messed with it, but I do know that it had some weird behavior when you mounted Cephfs directly instead of a NFS mount, etc...
- Likely ceph needs to be added to the existing list of `overlay` and `btrfs` to be handles specially here: https://github.com/sylabs/singularity/blob/974607a4fbe7288cc2cb73a8fb7688260d58881d/pkg/util/fs/proc/proc.go#L121
- That line of code is that way in the release-3.5 branch, not in the 3.5.2 tag. I am making a scratch epel rpm build for @username_0 with this change and will post here with a link when it is ready.
- Here is the [rpm version 3.5.2-1.1.1](https://kojipkgs.fedoraproject.org//work/tasks/5844/39945844/singularity-3.5.2-1.1.1.el7.x86_64.rpm). In addition to @username_2's suggested change, it includes PRs #4880 and #4881 beyond tag 3.5.2.
- Hi, I tested https://kojipkgs.fedoraproject.org//work/tasks/5844/39945844/singularity-3.5.2-1.1.1.el7.x86_64.rpm and it works. Thanks!
- Thanks @username_0 and @username_3 - PR #4922 has the small patch.

- Hi, Yeah. We eventually figured this out. The trick was how to tell puppet this. In the end we did this: ensure_packages( ['lustre-osd-ldiskfs', ‘kernel-2.6.32-504.8.1.el6_lustre.x86_64’], { before => Package['lustre'], } ) ensure_packages(['lustre']) And that seems to have settled matters and I hope this note gets googled by the next person whom encounters this ☺ Faye

Title:
dns_server multiple hosts with the same IP

Description:
Hello, When we generate the dns configuration, the same IP is defined for hostname and hostname-ice1-1 : ``` /var/named/forward:spartan198 IN A 10.10.1.150 /var/named/forward:spartan198-ice1-1 IN A 10.10.1.150 /var/named/reverse:172.16.58.3 IN PTR spartan198.bench.local. /var/named/reverse:172.16.58.3 IN PTR spartan198-ice1-1.bench.local. ``` IMHO we should use a CNAME to define spartan198-ice1-1 Some tools as shine are puzzled with the IP defined used for the hostname also used for a different "A" record. I'm testing this WA : * sed -i "s/\(spartan.*\)-ice1-1 IN A.*/\1-ice1-1 IN CNAME \1/" forward * sed -i "/spartan.*ice1-1/d" reverse

Comments:
- BTW, the new dns_server role requires python36-jmespath now.
- Hi @username_0 , The dependencies for Ansible are installed with the role core/ansible (will be renamed to core/bluebanquise soon).
- I'm thinking of a parameter `dns_server_zone_files = auto|static` for this role. With `auto`, the zone files are created from templates. With `static`, the zone files are copied from files, thus the admin can define the DNS zones with additional entries (CNAME, SRV, TXT, etc.). It would need a documentation of the mandatory entries (hostname, hostname-net).
- This approach is understandable, other roles should also allow such things. I am think for example to Slurm role. Base role provides a minimum working configuration, but often local administrator is tuning slurm.conf file. +1 on my side.
- Same +1
- Hi Bruno, I'm not talking about the capability to add custom entries/parameters/forwarders/zones in the dns configuration ( which is always a good idea to ease customisation), but the fact that a bmc IP ( or the management IP on ice1 for nodes ) is defined twice: we have 2 "A" records with the same IP It's not clear if it's a issue, a "well known High End stack" is also defining 2 hostnames for the same IP, but - I don't think it's RFC compliant - I don't know how to define nids/client in shine when two hostnames are returned by a nslookup
- Hi Gauthier, Yes, I understood your request. I read some RFC yesterday but did not find any rule that forbid to have several A records for a same IP address. Still searching. Note that named-checkzone return OK when testing the files. I don't understand the issue with shine, you can map your NIDs with one of the name: `nid_map: nodes=mds[1-2] nids=mds[1-2]-ib0@o2ib0` It should resolve to a single IP address per host and record the correct NID in the mgs. Ping me through another channel if you need additional help on this specific topic.
- Hi Bruno, I can't find restrictions in RFC too but I don't expect to receive different answer when I lookup for the hostname associated to a IP in this situation ( HPC ). CNAME seems to be a better practise in this case. For shine let me show you some outputs : ``` [root@spartan157 ~]# nslookup `gethostip -d $(hostname -s)` 192.168.3.11.in-addr.arpa name = spartan157-ice1-1.bench.local. 192.168.3.11.in-addr.arpa name = spartan157.bench.local. [root@spartan157 ~]# nslookup `gethostip -d $(hostname -s)` 192.168.3.11.in-addr.arpa name = spartan157.bench.local. 192.168.3.11.in-addr.arpa name = spartan157-ice1-1.bench.local. ``` Shine part : ``` #grep spartan /var/cache/shine/conf/lustrena.xmf client:node=spartan[0,100-363,400-415,500-559] nid_map:nids=spartan[0,100-363,400-415,500-559]-ib0@o2ib nodes=spartan[0,100-363,400-415,500-559] ``` ``` [root@spartan157 ~]# shine -L mount WARNING: Nothing to mount on spartan157-ice1-1 for `lustrena' WARNING: Nothing was done for `lustrena'. [root@spartan157 ~]# shine -L mount Load module 'lustre' ... Load module 'lustre': 'lustre' is already loaded ``` For shine, when we use -L it checks the hostname calling hostname_short . hostname_short uses socket.getfqdn which call gethostbyaddr() which return both hostnames, in "round-robin" order.... as far as I understand
- @username_0 @username_1 Is this issue solved on your side, or still open?
- I did not find time to dig further. My understanding of the issue so far is the shine tool is using reverse lookup to check if the configured IP address match the hostname. Thus, this is not an issue with multiple A records for a same IP address in the forward map, but with multiple PTR records for a same IP address in the reverse map. This is totally legit to have several PTR records for a single IP address (while not recommended for mail servers). If this is a design choice in BB, I don't see any reason to change it. Otherwise, the dns_server role could be updated to configure a single PTR record per IP address. One or the other, I don't mind.
- I am closing this issue, since everyone seems to have found a way to solve the issue, and that the issue is not coming from the stack itself.
- Hi, Could you please consider to re-open this issue : I'm configuring a IDM and from redhat manual we have : ``` Warning If a reverse DNS (PTR record) search returns multiple host names, httpd and other software associated with IdM may show unpredictable behavior. Red Hat strongly recommends configuring only one PTR record per IP. ``` https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/8/html/installing_identity_management/preparing-the-system-for-ipa-server-installation_installing-identity-management
